title: Detainee beaten, jury told; Police punched Dukic after he was restrained, witness tells inquest
article: Bryan Dukic was quickly subdued and did not strike the two officers who arrested him several hours before he died in custody, witnesses told a coroner's inquest Thursday.

Contrary to testimony from Const. Richard Sieberer and Const. John Ryan, who said Dukic was combative, striking one of the officers and ripping another's jacket, the civilian witnesses who watched the dramatic scene unfold from different vantage points said Dukic appeared to be under control within seconds.

Dukic, 42, was apprehended behind a Russell Street apartment building on April 5, 2006, after being identified as a disqualified driver with previous driving-related convictions. Following an altercation with the officers, his body became limp and he fell from a kneeling position while handcuffed, striking his head on the pavement. Dukic later died from a ruptured spleen and internal bleeding, caused by blunt force trauma and made worse by an existing medical condition -- cirrhosis of the liver and an abnormally large spleen.

Casey Willock, who watched the arrest from the patio of the nearby Dominion House tavern on Sandwich Street, told jurors that the officers chased Dukic in the grassy area next to a parking lot behind the building, knocking him to the ground. After a brief struggle, one of the officers managed to pull Dukic's hands behind his back and restrain them, Willock said. Even though Dukic was under control, the other officer stood up and delivered "at least four punches" to Dukic's head with "full force," he said.
Ryan testified Wednesday that he punched Dukic four or five times in the head because Dukic refused to give up his arms for handcuffing.
Willock testified that he was too far away to see whether handcuffs had been placed on Dukic's hands, but said there was "no question" that Dukic was restrained.
"The word that I would best use to describe it is 'disgusting,'" he said of the punching.

April Campbell-Logan, who lived at 3135 Russell St. at the time, said she watched the incident from her third-floor apartment window with her boyfriend and could see that "something was wrong" with Dukic after he was handcuffed, aside from the blood on his face.
"He did not look well," she said. "His stomach was really bloated ... sticking out. His colour started to change."
Campbell-Logan said she looked away from her window a few times, but did not see Dukic strike either officer.

Dukic's friend, Brian Lacroix, who was a passenger in the Dodge Caravan Dukic was driving, testified that Dukic did not run from the officers. Ryan approached Dukic from behind, grabbed one of his arms and threw him to the ground, he said.
"These guys had him down like that. There was no swearing, nothing. Just bang, bang," Lacroix testified.

But the lawyer for the two police officers and the Windsor Police Service, Nancy Jammu-Taylor, said Lacroix gave a much different statement to police the day of the incident, saying Dukic was resisting arrest and his arms "were flying all over."

When the struggle was over, Lacroix said he was told he could leave the scene. Lacroix asked if he could grab his case of OV beer from the back of the van and walked past Dukic, who he said was laying on the ground motionless, his eyes closed.

Crystal Chevalier, who saw parts of the incident from her seventh-floor balcony at 3165 Russell St., said she saw one of the officers "nudge" Dukic with his foot while the handcuffed detainee lay on the ground, "maybe to check to see if he was OK."

The inquest is being held to determine the circumstances of Dukic's death -- mandatory when someone dies while in custody. An investigation by the province's Special Investigations Unit cleared Sieberer and Ryan of any wrongdoing in 2006, concluding they used reasonable force against Dukic.
